prompt.context: Our client is Thompson Healthcare, a health insurance firm located in the Midwest. Customers pay Thompson a fixed monthly premium per person covered under the plan. In exchange, Thompson pays for all health services that each member requires (e.g., physician care, prescription medications, hospitalization). In recent years, Thompson's financial and competitive position has begun to erode, and the CEO has retained our firm to help them determine what is causing the problem and how to fix it.
prompt.question: How can Thompson Healthcare reduce its total cost to serve its policyholders?

clarifying_info.q: Is Thompson a for-profit or non-profit insurer?
clarifying_info.a: Thompson is a mutual insurance company — all profits are returned to members as lower premiums the following year. It seeks to minimize cost, not maximize profit.

clarifying_info.q: How does Thompson price its policies?
clarifying_info.a: Prices reflect underwriting of risk and the underlying cost to serve a customer.
Market share is steady despite competition from a major national insurer, United Healthcare (UHC). UHC holds 30% market share and targets a 5% profit margin.

clarifying_info.q: What is the trend in medical cost inflation?
clarifying_info.a: The national average rate of medical cost inflation is 10% over the past five years. Thompson has seen 12% medical cost inflation; UHC has seen 10%.

clarifying_info.q: How many members does Thompson have?

clarifying_info.a: Policies are sold through independent agents. All independent agents work with a General Agency, which acts as a sales support organization.
Commission is 10% of annual premiums, paid to the General Agency, which passes a share to the independent agent. On average this equals $25 per member per month.

exhibits.title: Problem Structure
exhibits.shows: A framework slide outlining the key elements to analyze — cost structure broken into variable (medical) costs and fixed (administrative) costs
exhibits.data: Variable costs: medical costs (claims); Fixed costs: administrative costs (marketing & sales, underwriting, finance, HR)

exhibits.title: Initial Hypothesis — Medical Costs
exhibits.shows: A slide posing the hypothesis about medical cost inflation being above the national average, with the formula Medical cost = Number of claims x Cost per claim
exhibits.data: Medical cost formula: Number of claims x Cost per claim; Thompson medical cost inflation: 12%; National average: 10%

exhibits.title: Second Hypothesis — Administrative / Sales Costs
exhibits.shows: A slide describing Thompson's sales channel through independent agents and General Agencies, presenting information to calculate total commission expense and evaluate approaches to reduce cost of sales
exhibits.data: Commission rate: 10% of annual premiums; Average commission: $25 per member per month; Members: 500,000

exhibits.title: Next Level of Analysis — General Agency Fee Split
exhibits.shows: A slide describing the three activities performed by General Agencies (training, application processing, performance management) and their internal cost equivalents, to determine the maximum fee Thompson should pay General Agencies under the new flat-commission structure
exhibits.data: Training internal cost: $6,000,000; Application processing internal cost: $9,000,000; Performance management internal cost: $15,000,000; Total: $30,000,000; Members: 500,000

framework: Identify the two main cost drivers: variable (medical claims) costs and fixed (administrative) costs
Analyze medical costs using the formula: Medical cost = Number of claims x Cost per claim
Benchmark Thompson's medical cost inflation (12%) against national average (10%) to identify the gap
Analyze administrative costs, focusing on the largest driver: cost of sales through the independent agent / General Agency channel
Quantify total commission expense and evaluate structural options to reduce it
Synthesize findings into prioritized recommendations to the CEO

questions.prompt: What factors would you consider to understand Thompson's eroding financial position?
questions.guidance: Candidate should focus on costs (not revenue, since Thompson is a mutual insurer seeking to minimize cost). Costs split into: (1) Variable costs = medical costs (claims by policyholders) and (2) Fixed costs = administrative costs (marketing & sales, underwriting, finance, HR). Candidate should note that Thompson's medical cost inflation (12%) exceeds the national average (10%) and UHC's rate (10%), making medical costs the primary area of investigation.

questions.prompt: Medical costs are the largest component of Thompson's costs and are increasing faster than the national average. What are some potential reasons why this is taking place, and what opportunities could reverse this trend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should break down medical costs as: Medical cost = Number of claims x Cost per claim. Strong answers will generate hypotheses across both drivers. Number of claims drivers: low deductibles prompt members to seek care for minor issues (raise deductibles); Thompson insures an older population (market more to younger customers); Thompson insures a sicker population (enhance wellness programs). Cost per claim drivers: Thompson pays more per procedure than competitors (conduct benchmarking study on procedure prices). Candidate should identify at least 3-4 distinct hypotheses.

math.setup: Medical cost = Number of claims x Cost per claim
steps: Identify whether the gap is driven by claim volume, claim price, or both
Benchmark against UHC and national averages on each dimension
math.answer: No single numerical answer; the goal is generating hypotheses and prioritization.

questions.prompt: How much does Thompson pay in commissions each year? What approaches could reduce cost of sales, and what strategic risks do they carry?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate total annual commission: $25 per member per month x 500,000 members x 12 months = $150,000,000. Approaches to reduce: (1) Reduce commission percentage; (2) Cap commission at a ceiling per year; (3) Change from percentage-of-premium to flat fee per member per month (percentage-of-premium rises with medical cost inflation, compounding costs). Strategic risks: agents could shift business to carriers paying higher commissions; capping commissions removes incentive to sell. UHC pays a flat commission per member per month — candidate should note this as a benchmark supporting option 3.

math.setup: Total commission = Commission per member per month x Members x Months per year

questions.prompt: The team has decided to pay a flat commission directly to agents and a separate fee to General Agencies for support services. If total commission to both parties is $20 per member per month, what share should go to the General Agencies?
questions.guidance: Candidate should derive the maximum willingness-to-pay for General Agency services by calculating what it would cost Thompson to perform those activities internally. Training ($6M) + Application processing ($9M) + Performance management ($15M) = $30M total. Convert to per-member-per-month: $30,000,000 / (500,000 x 12) = $5 per member per month. Therefore General Agencies should receive at most $5 per member per month, leaving $15 per member per month for agents. This is an economic value / make-vs-buy analysis.

math.setup: Max General Agency fee = Internal cost of activities / (Members x Months)
math.answer: Maximum of $5 per member per month to General Agencies; $15 per member per month to agents

brainstorming.prompt: What initiatives would you recommend to the CEO to reduce Thompson's total cost to serve policyholders?

categories.name: Medical cost reduction
ideas: Enhance marketing to attract younger, healthier members to lower average claims per member
Conduct benchmarking study to identify where Thompson overpays for procedures vs. competitors and negotiate lower rates
Increase deductibles so members are more cost-conscious about seeking care for minor issues
Invest in wellness programs to improve population health and reduce claim frequency

categories.name: Administrative / sales cost reduction
ideas: Switch commission structure from percentage-of-premium to flat fee per member per month to decouple commissions from medical cost inflation
Set General Agency fee at or below $5 per member per month (economic value of their services) and pay agents the remainder of the $20 flat fee
Evaluate internalizing one or more General Agency functions (training, application processing, performance management) if internal cost is lower

categories.name: Broader strategic considerations
ideas: Monitor agent retention and channel loyalty after commission restructuring — mitigate defection risk
Benchmark administrative cost ratios against UHC and national peers to identify further savings
Consider longer-term direct-to-consumer or digital sales channels to reduce reliance on agent commissions

recommendation: Reduce medical cost inflation to the national average (10%) by: attracting younger/healthier members through targeted marketing, conducting a procedure-cost benchmarking study to negotiate provider rates down, increasing deductibles, and enhancing wellness programs

Restructure the sales commission from a percentage-of-premium model to a flat fee of $20 per member per month — capped at $5 per member per month for General Agencies (reflecting the economic value of their support services) and $15 per member per month for agents — saving $5 per member per month vs. the current $25, or $30,000,000 per year in commission savings
risks: Independent agents may shift business to higher-commission carriers if the flat fee is perceived as a pay cut
Capping General Agency fees could reduce quality or responsiveness of agent support services
Higher deductibles may cause member attrition if competitively differentiated
Wellness programs require upfront investment with uncertain ROI timeline
next_steps: Conduct agent satisfaction and retention analysis before implementing commission changes
Commission a procedure-cost benchmarking study comparing Thompson vs. UHC and regional peers
Model the demographic mix of Thompson's insured population to size the marketing opportunity for younger members
Develop an implementation roadmap with phased rollout of commission restructuring to manage agent relations
